content.overview: Section 80 CPC requires two months' written notice before a suit against the Government or a public officer for an act purporting to be done in official capacity, unless the court permits an urgent-relief suit under sub-section (2).
content.study: Name the authority, state the cause of action, identify the plaintiff, and state the relief. Serve the notice. Wait two months unless urgency is pleaded and the court grants leave. Want of notice is often visible on the plaint and can support Order VII rule 11 if the exemption is not properly pleaded. Do not treat a writ petition as a Section 80 suit.
